verdict.rationale: Paddle documents webhook push notifications signed with a `Paddle-Signature` header and a shared secret. Its Node.js and Python SDKs ship signature-verification helpers, and an IP allowlist is recommended. The evidence never documents automatic webhook redelivery, an event/delivery log, or replay; payment dunning retries are a different capability and are not credited. Missing for 10: automatic webhook delivery retries, webhook event/delivery logs, event replay/redelivery, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on signed webhook deliveries with automatic retries, event logs, and replay to keep my system consistent with payment state

citations.quote: Paddle uses webhooks to push real-time notifications to your server when things happen in your account.
All webhooks sent by Paddle include a `Paddle-Signature` header. Paddle generates this header using a secret key that only you and Paddle know.
It ships with TypeScript definitions, iterator-based pagination, and helpers for webhook signature verification.
includes a webhook signature verifier that works with Flask, Django, and anything speaking the request protocol.
